title: ERIS UI/UX Redesign Plan (web client) v1.1
summary: ERIS's web client fails newcomers for one reason: a person must learn five numbered objects (Incident, Event Group, Assessment, Submission, cross-section Project) across six read-only record pages plus a separate action inbox before doing anything. Measured on main @ 727024e: the first 700px of /my-work, /incidents and /assessments is navigation on both a 375px phone and a 768px iPad; the Staff technical form is 11.1 screens tall with 180 overflowing elements, 120 controls under 40px and 74 text nodes under 12px; of 15 first-day tasks, 4 were blocked and 4 confusing. The direction is Inbox + Case file. Every role, including the maintenance field reporter, gets a personal Home grouped by the action they must take, with rows that lead with the site rather than three internal ids. What changes per role after the owner's routing decisions: the office chief's Home is grouped To route / To review and the hand-off becomes one step with two choices - hand off to a branch chief, or assign a GeoTech Senior Engineer directly, with no third choice - the office chief cannot assign Staff directly; the branch chief now approves the assessments handed to them, so there is no reviewer to assign and no sign-off after; and a new GeoTech Senior Engineer role fills assessments the office chief assigns directly and returns them to that chief. Approval ends the assessment, review authority follows the assessment's routing path rather than an assignment or an account role, and the district coordinator is notified in-app and by email when an assessment is approved. /incidents/:id becomes the only record page, with assessment, technical form, evidence, site and history as tabs; no backend object is renamed, and the only state-machine change is the owner routing decision: approval becomes terminal and finalize is retired (B15). Navigation collapses to at most four destinations per role, rendered as a bottom bar on phones, an 80px labelled rail with 12px labels on iPads and a 256px sidebar on desktops. Every hand-off becomes a route-backed guided flow that is a full page below md and a centred dialog from md, states its consequence before the button, holds that action's note and leaves a receipt. v1.1 closes four classes of defect found in build-readiness review: the reporter now has a Home and a route-backed Update-your-report flow (/incidents/:id/update) that calls the PATCH /incidents/{id} endpoint that already exists and already enforces requested-fields-only, so the coordinator's 'ask the reporter' disposition no longer commits into a dead end; every full-height composition is re-costed against the measured 1097px main at 1440, so the three-region form is container-queried at 1240px of workspace rather than assumed from a breakpoint, and no route stacks a bottom nav bar under an action bar; the feature flag moves to a build-time Vite variable because parse_user_metadata whitelists three keys and drops the rest, and two new backend items are added for per-account UI preferences and the Home queue filters that six Home groups had no data source for; and every page spec now carries phone, tablet and desktop layouts plus an empty state, with three new specs for Not Found, access sharing and the reporter's update flow. Seven phases, 73 working days of calendar for two front-end engineers, two backend engineers full-time for Phase 1 and then one at roughly a third of their time, a designer at half time and QA at half time from Phase 3 - 137 front-end engineer-days and 37.75 backend engineer-days; Phase 1 carries 21.5 backend engineer-days, which one third-time engineer would spend 64 calendar days on rather than 11. Three backend items gate: B1 (one transaction driving assessment and submission), B12 (Home queue filters) and B3 (the case aggregate) - and two new ones, B15 (routing v2) and B16 (the approval email), gate Phase 1 with them. Of the two items previously listed as backend work, B2 is moot because there is no finalize list, and B10 already ships server-side and is client-only.

principles.name: One place per incident
principles.statement: Everything about an incident lives at /incidents/:id; assessment, technical form, evidence, site and history are tabs, never destinations. Legacy record URLs still resolve and render the same case file entered on the right tab.
principles.codeReviewTest: A new top-level <Route> rendering a record detail that is not /incidents/:id, /assessments/:id, /submissions/:id or /event-groups/:id is rejected.

principles.name: One banner, one button, no redirection
principles.statement: Every object page and tab opens with one Next-step banner: plain status, holder (a named person, or 'you'), one sentence on what happens after the action, and one primary button. No page ever tells the user to act somewhere else.
principles.codeReviewTest: Grep the diff for 'in My Work', 'performed from', 'actions live in' in user-visible copy — any hit fails. Assert exactly one element with data-primary-action per rendered route.

principles.name: Place before ids
principles.statement: Every row, card, banner, title and map popup leads with the incident title and the shared location string ('District 7 · Los Angeles · Route 101 · PM 12.30'). Numeric ids appear once, muted, at the end. Codes never appear.
principles.codeReviewTest: Rendering #{id} before the title, or interpolating office_code / current_stage / state / a role code / a section key into user text, fails. Everything goes through the labels module.

principles.name: Only what this page decides
principles.statement: Each screen carries only the data its decision needs. Three tiers of disclosure and only three: expandable row, drawer or bottom sheet, overflow menu. Never nest disclosure beyond two levels; never put units, requirements or a disabled reason behind hover.
principles.codeReviewTest: Max 5 facts per row; max 4 data columns at md, 6 at xl, cards below md. A row's single action column holds controls, not facts, and does not count against the data-column budget - but there is at most one of it and it never carries text a user must read. Any title= carrying information not also visible fails.

principles.name: Compose per width, never shrink
principles.statement: Tailwind's stock breakpoints; each gets a designed composition. Below md: bottom bar, single pane, sheets. md: 80px rail, single pane. lg+: two panes, for Home and Map only. A third region is container-queried at 1240px of workspace width, never assumed from a breakpoint - the measured main at 1440 with the sidebar pinned is 1097px.
principles.codeReviewTest: nestedScrollRegions === 0 vertical below lg, <= 1 at lg+, plus at most one horizontal scroll-snap chip strip at any width, each marked data-scroll-region='pane' or 'chips'. mainContentStartsAtPx <= 64 below md, <= 120 above. bottomBarCount <= 1 on every route. New max-h-[Npx] overflow-auto without data-scroll-region fails.

principles.name: Consequence before commit, receipt after
principles.statement: Anything that changes ownership, notifies someone or cannot be undone opens a sheet naming the target and person, stating the consequence in one sentence, holding that action's note, focusing Cancel when destructive; on success a persistent notice says what happened and where it went. Nothing ever vanishes silently.
principles.codeReviewTest: Every call site of delegateBranch, assignSeniorEngineer, assignEngineer, addAssignment, submit, review, resolve, triage, resubmitIncident, disableUser, resetPassword, deleteSubmission, grantAccess, revokeAccess and publishVersion must sit inside a confirm surface and pass a message to the notice region.

principles.name: Never disable a primary silently
principles.statement: A primary is never disabled without its reason in the same sentence position. Where the block is incompleteness, the button stays live and opens a completeness sheet linking to what is missing. Where the block is policy - you cannot disable your own account, or the last administrator - the reason is visible text beside the control and the button opens a sheet carrying it.
principles.codeReviewTest: disabled on a primary without an adjacent visible reason fails. 'Send for review' is never disabled.

navigation.model: Four destinations at most, per role. 1) Home - what needs me; the landing page for every role including reporters, with a count badge. 2) Records - look something up; three segments (Incidents, Event Groups, Assessments) and no badge; for reporters a single list titled 'My reports'. 3) Map - where is it (renamed from Mission Center; the name 'Mission Center' survives only inside the per-record Technical details disclosure). 4) One role-specific fourth: Admin, or Terrain for Staff and senior engineers, the only personas whose top task begins there. Plus an avatar menu and a Help button in the same header slot on every page (SC 3.2.6). Everything else stops being a destination: assessments and technical forms are case-file tabs, Terrain opens from the case file for everyone else, Settings lives in the avatar menu, and access sharing is a flow route off the technical form. Two contradictions between proposals are resolved on the record: Records keeps an Event Groups segment because the coordinator's first triage decision is an event decision and Event Group carries the highest confusion rating; and Records keeps an Assessments segment for chiefs, but selecting a row opens the case file's 'Who has it' tab, so there is exactly one record detail surface in the product.
navigation.desktop: 1280-1535: a 256px sidebar, collapsible to the rail, and defaulting to the rail on form and case-file routes with the choice remembered. Two panes. A third region appears only where the workspace itself measures at least 1240px, which is a container query and not a breakpoint: index 200 + form 720 + pane 320 + two 24px gaps is 1288px, so at 1280 with the rail the workspace is 1152px and it does not appear. Measured outcomes: 1440 with the sidebar pinned is 1097px so two regions; 1440 with the rail is 1312px so three; 1600 with the sidebar is 1296px so three. 1536 and above adds no new regions beyond that rule; the shell is capped at 1600px and dense pages at 1440px, and extra width reveals priority-3 columns and widens panes, never cells.
navigation.tablet: 768-1023 (iPad portrait, the primary field width): a persistent 80px labelled icon rail - 24px icon, 4px gap, a 12px label (never 10px; a navigation label is essential text and the plan's own floor is 12px), 56px items with a 44px hit area, active brand-filled with aria-current. No bottom bar, no stacked nav card, no hamburger. Rail plus a single pane with drill-in, about 656px of content; supporting map and photos are a bottom sheet at 40/90 percent snaps, not a second column. A 44px title row carries h1 left and the primary action right. Dialogs become centred panels at this width - md is the single dialog breakpoint. 1024-1279 (iPad landscape): the same rail with a pinnable 256px sidebar; two panes switch on here for Home and Map only. The case file stays a single pane with its tab strip, because 1024 minus the 80px rail and padding leaves about 896px and a 320px queue would leave about 540px for a banner, key facts, a progress rail and a supporting pane.
navigation.phone: Under 640px: a 56px header (menu-or-back, title, avatar), a 56px bottom tab bar (--bottom-nav-h) and safe-area padding. On any :id, flow or section route the bottom nav bar is replaced by a back control naming the parent plus one sticky action bar - bars never stack. The one nav destination that needs an action bar, /terrain, has the action bar replace the nav bar and puts a Home control in the header. Every full-height container subtracts every bar on its route: /map is calc(100svh - --header-h - --segment-h - --bottom-nav-h - env(safe-area-inset-bottom)). The nav bar hides only when the soft keyboard is up, detected as visualViewport.height shrinking by more than 120px - never on focus alone, because on iPadOS with a hardware keyboard the viewport does not shrink. Single pane with drill-in; tables become cards; dialogs are full-screen sheets; maps are a tab or a sheet, never inside page scroll. The 640-767 band keeps this shell deliberately: md is Tailwind's switch and we do not add a custom one, so the iPad half-split at 678px gets a labelled bottom bar rather than a rail.

rules: Keep Tailwind v4's stock breakpoints (sm 640, md 768, lg 1024, xl 1280, 2xl 1536). Do not add an @theme block to override them: the proposed 480/600/840/1200/1440 remap silently reinterprets 136 existing utilities across ~50 screens in one atomic release, in a codebase with no DOM tests in CI, for no user-visible gain.

Export the same numbers from web/src/ui/breakpoints.ts for matchMedia hooks (useBreakpoint) used by ArcGIS sizing and the Map | List control. Never key layout to a user-agent or device name — always the viewport or the container.

Use Tailwind v4 container queries for everything panel-internal: @container on the detail pane, supporting pane, dialog body, toolbar and table wrapper, then @sm:…@5xl: on children. A pane's own width, not the viewport, decides whether a pipeline is horizontal or a column is visible, because the sidebar can be pinned or collapsed.

Measure four heights with one ResizeObserver hook onto documentElement, each with a static fallback: --header-h (56), --bottom-nav-h (56), --action-bar-h (44), --segment-h (44), plus --panel-h for split layouts. Use them in top-, scroll-mt- and every calc(100svh - ...). Delete the magic top-[82px] at AppShell.tsx:166.

Use svh for map and SceneView containers and dvh for everything else that must fit with the mobile URL bar and keyboard; add viewport-fit=cover to the viewport meta. dvh changes as the iOS URL bar collapses, which resizes the ArcGIS view on every scroll frame; svh is the stable small viewport. Debounce the ArcGIS resize handler at 150ms regardless.

Every interactive element is at least 24×24 CSS px with 8px spacing, and at least 44×44px hit area under @media (pointer: coarse) via pointer-coarse:min-h-11 min-w-11 on Button, nav items, row actions, chips, checkboxes wrapped in a 44px label, ArcGIS view.ui widgets, 3D controls, pipeline steps and dialog closes. Rows are 48px on coarse pointers and 40px on fine.
No essential text below 12px, navigation labels included - which is why the iPad rail label is 12px and not 10px. Body 14px, table cells 13-14px, 16px on phone form inputs to prevent iOS zoom.

No hover-only affordances. The justification is NOT that Tailwind scopes hover: inside @media (hover:hover): the real hover affordance in this codebase is hand-written CSS at index.css:132 (.attachment-tile:hover .attachment-tile-actions), which no Tailwind scoping touches, and it already ships a @media (hover: none) override at index.css:138-142 plus :focus-within, so the pure-touch case is handled today. The residual case is the hybrid pointer: an iPad with a Magic Keyboard trackpad reports hover: hover while the user taps the glass. The rule is therefore that any control which must be discoverable is always visible, and :hover only ever emphasises something already rendered. Links are underlined.
Selected and active state is never colour alone: aria-current (nav and selected rows), aria-pressed (toggle chips), plus a visible check glyph or a 2px brand border.

Every drag has a tap and keyboard alternative: the form canvas drag/resize is deleted; cross-section control points can be removed and zoomed from the Points list; the supporting-pane resize handle answers ArrowLeft/Right.
Maps on coarse pointers require gesture opt-in (an 'Enable map gestures' affordance or a two-finger pan requirement) so a finger scrolling the page is never captured by an inline map.

Outside the page scroll a screen may have at most ONE vertical scroll region - a sticky rail at lg+, a sheet body, a dialog body, or a table's horizontal wrapper - PLUS at most one horizontal scroll-snap chip strip. Each carries tabIndex={0}, an edge fade and data-scroll-region ('pane' or 'chips'). A chip strip is allowed only if it is 48px tall or less and every destination in it is also reachable from a non-scrolling control on the same screen: the form hub's section list for the section chip strip, the More menu for the case-file cross-link row. The phone form-section page therefore has no chip strip at all - its sticky bottom bar carries Back and Save and continue. The max-h-[860/760/520/420px] caps are deleted.

Bars never stack. A route shows either the bottom NAV bar or one sticky ACTION bar, never both, at any width. On :id, flow and section routes the nav bar is replaced by a back control in the header plus the action bar. On a nav destination that needs an action bar - /terrain is the only one - the action bar REPLACES the nav bar and the header's left slot becomes a Home control (--action-bar-h 44px). Every full-height container subtracts every bar above and below it: /map is calc(100svh - --header-h - --segment-h - --bottom-nav-h - env(safe-area-inset-bottom)); /terrain is calc(100svh - --header-h - --action-bar-h - env(safe-area-inset-bottom)). Bottom bars are min-h-14 pb-[env(safe-area-inset-bottom)]. The nav bar hides only when the soft keyboard is up, detected as visualViewport.height shrinking by more than 120px - never on focus alone, because on iPadOS with a hardware keyboard the visual viewport does not shrink and navigation would disappear for no reason.

MapView and SceneView are never inside a scrolling container; popups dock bottom-centre below md; markers are 1.5x with 44px hit areas on coarse pointers; clustering only above district scale; never view.goTo on a poll tick or a filter keystroke. One MapView per mounted map and never two on one screen: the Map destination keeps a single view alive in its layout route, while embedded maps (case-file site map, triage candidates, photo map) each own a view created on mount and destroyed on unmount. Where a flow would put two on screen at once, the flow is a full-screen route below md and, from md, a dialog that detaches the underlying view (view.container = null) while open and reattaches on close. ArcGIS views are never shared between two mounted panes.

Never put position or z-index on the global .esri-view class; keep the isolation-only rule and wrap every view in .map-stack-guard. z-index scale: header 20, sticky sub-toolbar 10, rail 10, bottom nav 30, drawer/sheet 40, dialog 50, full-screen 3D 60.

Flex/grid overflow hygiene: min-w-0 on every flex child holding text or a table; grid columns minmax(0,1fr) never bare 1fr; delete fixed min-widths above ~277px (min-w-[280px] search, min-w-72 card, min-w-[520px] chart) in favour of w-full min-w-0 with the fixed width only from the breakpoint where it fits.

At 320px width and 400% zoom, headers, filters, search, form fields, dialogs, cards and the Next-step banner must not scroll horizontally; only whole tables and maps may, inside wrappers that are keyboard-reachable and labelled.
Honour prefers-reduced-motion for map goTo animations, marker highlight, sheet and drawer transitions, skeleton shimmer and the 3D camera fly-to.
Scroll-spy on the form index uses IntersectionObserver with fixed section anchors — a scroll-position implementation jitters on iPad Safari with dynamic content heights.

Delete on landing: submissionLayoutModel.ts, useSubmissionDashboardLayout.ts, the aside lg:hidden nav card in AppShell.tsx:164, the product-card overflow-hidden wrapper around main's children at AppShell.tsx:185 (it defeats position: sticky for every sticky index, sub-toolbar and action bar the layout system relies on), the max-w-[1900px] shell cap at AppShell.tsx:140,163,189 (replaced by the 1600px cap), the nested max-h caps, min-w-[74px] pipeline steps, max-w-[calc(100%-360px)], the 1200px colgroup, and the raw role codes at AppShell.tsx:157.

A third region is container-queried at 1240px of workspace width, never assumed from a breakpoint. The measured main at 1440 with the 256px sidebar is 1097px (brief-core.md desktop_1440x900), so the three-region form composition - index 200 + form 720 + pane 320 + gaps = 1288px - never fits at 1280 and does not fit at 1440 with the sidebar pinned. Use @[1240px] on the workspace container and default the sidebar to the rail on form and case-file routes.

Two panes at lg apply to Home and Map only. The case file stays a single pane with its tab strip at every width until the 1240px container threshold: 1024 minus the 80px rail and padding is about 896px, and a 300-340px queue would leave about 540px for a banner, key facts, a progress rail and a supporting pane.

The Next-step banner clamps a quoted reviewer comment to four lines with 'Read the full comment' linking to the History anchor where it is quoted in full, so a long comment can never push the case-file tab strip or the primary action below the fold on a 375x812 screen. mainContentStartsAtPx does not catch this; the new primaryActionVisibleAtScrollZero assertion does.

onboarding: No welcome tour, coach-mark carousel or video. Staff rotate and touch ERIS only during events; tours are skipped, not remembered, and show no measured performance gain. The whole budget goes into the items below.

First-run 'How your work flows' card, once per account, dismissible and always recallable from Help: 3-5 steps in the plain status vocabulary with the user's own step highlighted (Coordinator: Report filed -> You review -> GeoTech assesses -> Approved -> Resolved). Admins get 'Where things get stuck' instead.

A Help panel in the same header slot on every page (WCAG 2.2 SC 3.2.6) with three tabs: How your work flows, Words used in ERIS (the vocabulary table filtered to terms on the current page first), and Contact GeoTech support. Side sheet on desktop and iPad landscape, bottom sheet on phones, never covering the primary action bar.

Empty states carry the teaching: every queue and list says why it is empty, what will appear there, and offers one action. This replaces onboarding prose repeated on every item, such as the triage explanatory paragraph and the 'Read-only record view' banner.

Just-in-time definitions instead of a glossary tour: the first time a session shows Event Group, ERIS number, Route this assessment, Returned for changes or GeoTech office, the term renders with a dotted underline and a tap or click info popover. Never hover-only, because the primary device is an iPad.

Status chips are tap-to-open ON DETAIL PAGES AND INSIDE THE NEXT-STEP BANNER ONLY. In list rows the chip is inert text, because the pattern ladder makes the whole card one link of at least 64px and a tappable popover trigger nested inside a link is ambiguous to tap and invalid to nest. In lists the definition lives on ONE info button per group header, outside every card. This is the contextual-help mechanic across the product.

Exactly two coach marks, once per account. The coordinator's first review flow: 'Pick the site this report belongs to - nothing is saved until you press Accept and send.' (v1.0 taught 'Record decision', a control the merged triage flow deletes.) The Staff member's first form: 'Sections can be completed in any order; your work autosaves.' Nothing else earns one. WHY THESE TWO ARE EXEMPT from the no-coach-marks finding at brief-research.md:37: that finding is about FRONT-LOADED tours and carousels shown before the user has a task. These are single, in-context marks that appear inside the one irreversible flow in the product at the moment the user is in it, and each states a fact the interface cannot show - that nothing has been written yet, and that order does not matter. If the Phase 2 walkthrough shows either is ignored, it is deleted rather than reworded.

Success confirmations as onboarding: after every workflow action a persistent notice names the object, the new state and where it went ('Assessment for ERIS no. 24-0417 handed off to Maria Chen. It has left your queue and is now under Records > Assessments.') with 'Open it' and Undo where the backend allows. People learn the flow by doing it.

Consequence-stating confirmations for irreversible steps (Close - no assessment, Link and close, Route this assessment, Approve, Return for changes, Mark resolved, Disable user, Publish or Restore Road Inventory): one sentence of consequence, the note field inside the dialog, Cancel receiving initial focus, and the primary disabled only while submitting.

Rotating-staff return path: an account with no sign-in for 60 or more days sees the 'How your work flows' card once more, and 'Recently done by me (7 days)' stays collapsed on Home so people can see where their last actions went. This is driven by last_sign_in_at, which B11 adds to /auth/me; without it the return path has no trigger.

Role labels are onboarding: the header shows one humanised primary role, the avatar menu lists all roles with one-line descriptions, and the Users admin page shows the same descriptions beside each role so admins provision correctly.

Where the 'once per account' state lives: items 1 and 5, the banner-dismissal memory, the Records-assessments first-visit hint, the pane width, the list-pane state, theme and density all need a per-user store, and THERE IS NONE TODAY - UiSettingsContext writes localStorage, so on the shared field iPads the last person's state wins and every 'once per account' promise misfires. B11 adds GET/PUT /users/me/ui-preferences and last_sign_in_at; until it lands all of these degrade to localStorage and the UI says so ('Stored in this browser only').

The reporter gets onboarding of their own, not one row in a status table: a first-run card reading 'File -> Coordinator reviews -> They may ask you for more -> Accepted', a Home group named Needs your update, and an update flow that quotes the coordinator's question and lists exactly the fields they asked for.
accessibility: Target size (SC 2.5.8 AA): every interactive element at least 24x24 CSS px with 8px spacing, and at least 44x44px hit area under @media (pointer: coarse) - rail cards, table row actions, filter and role chips, attachment tile buttons, ArcGIS view.ui widgets sized via CSS, 3D scene controls, pipeline steps, dialog closes and 'Remove file'. Baseline: 120 failing controls on /submissions/3 alone. Baseline: 120 controls under 40px on /submissions/3 alone - brief-core.md:9 defines smallTapTargets at a 40px threshold, so the baseline is a 40px count and the metrics table says so rather than presenting it as a 44px count. Phase 0 re-measures the baseline at 44px so before and after use one threshold.

Text contrast, light theme (SC 1.4.3): --brand #1f9bd1, --good #1d9d5d and --bad #d14b54 on white or --panel-soft measure roughly 3.0-4.0:1 and FAIL 4.5:1 for 11-13px badge text and for white text on .btn-brand. Add per-theme text tokens: --good-text (at least #157a47), --bad-text (at least #b0303a), and a --warn BASE token plus --warn-text, because index.css defines no --warn today - that is two new tokens, not one. On --brand-text: the value already exists under another name. index.css:18 defines --brand-ink: #0e4c6a in light - the exact value v1.0 proposed for a new --brand-text - but :35 defines it as #e4f0ff in dark and :52 as #063e42 in coastal, so the token means ink ON a brand surface, a different job from brand-coloured text on a page surface. Do not overload it: add --brand-text as a separate token whose light value is #0e4c6a, and document the two roles side by side in the token file. Keep the light hues for 3:1 borders and icons only.

Dark theme: verify --line #233a61 on --panel #0f1d33 reaches 3:1 for form-field boundaries (SC 1.4.11); it likely fails. Add a --line-strong token for input borders and focus rings. Coastal theme: brand, good and bad pass, but do not use --muted #4f7280 on --panel-soft below 12px.
The contrast report is generated from the token file at build time so a theme change cannot regress it silently.

Minimum text size: no essential UI text below 12px (baseline 74 tiny nodes on the form page, 23 on /my-work); body 14px, table cells 13-14px, 16px on phone inputs; everything reflows at 200% zoom without clipping.

Status is never conveyed by colour alone (SC 1.4.1): every chip carries a text label, map markers encode status by shape plus colour plus label with a legend of only visible operational symbols, and the current pipeline step carries the word 'Now' plus aria-current='step'.

Focus visible and not obscured (SC 2.4.7, 2.4.11): a 2px --brand ring on every control, rail card and link; sticky headers and action bars must not cover the focused element - use scroll-margin-top equal to the header height and no nested fixed-height scrollers that hide focus.

Keyboard path for every map (SC 2.1.1): every map view has a same-page list or table with the same records and filters; row selection highlights the marker and vice versa; ArcGIS keyboard navigation is kept, the container has tabIndex=0 and an aria-label; popups open with an explicit Open button; no action is marker-only.

Keyboard path for canvas and 3D (SC 2.1.1, 2.1.2): the terrain profile SVG is focusable with ArrowLeft/ArrowRight (Shift for x10) stepping and tap-to-pin; control points are editable from a list (Remove, Zoom to) and coordinates can be typed; the SceneView is progressive enhancement with the elevation table and 2D map as the equivalent; Escape returns focus to the toolbar with no keyboard trap inside ArcGIS widgets.

Pointer gestures and dragging (SC 2.5.1, 2.5.7): mouse-only drag and resize is removed from the technical form; any remaining drag has a single-pointer and keyboard alternative; pinch and pan on a map inside a scrolling page must not trap scrolling on touch.

Reflow (SC 1.4.10): at 320px width and 400% zoom, headers, filters, form fields, dialogs, cards and the Next-step card never scroll horizontally; only whole data tables and maps may, inside overflow-x-auto containers with tabIndex=0, a visible cut-off and an aria-label.
Reduced motion (SC 2.3.3): honour prefers-reduced-motion for map goTo animations (animate:false), marker flash and highlight, drawer and sheet slide-ins, skeleton shimmer and the 3D camera fly-to.

Live regions: one polite region for autosave status, queue reloads and success notices; role='alert' for errors and 'Could not save'; aria-busy on panels while a record loads; never announce on every keystroke.

Names and roles: every input, select and search has a programmatic label; icon buttons have aria-label; tab strips use role=tablist/tab with aria-selected; tables have a caption and aria-sort on sortable headers; dialogs use role=dialog with aria-modal, labelled-by, a focus trap, Escape and focus return - the existing ModalDialog does this and the Save cross-section and Aerial capture dialogs must adopt it.

Page identity and navigation (SC 3.2.3, 3.2.4, 3.2.6): document.title per route ('Assessment - ERIS no. 24-0417 - ERIS'); a skip-to-content link; aria-current='page' on nav; a breadcrumb on record pages; and the Help control in the same location on every page.

Forms (SC 3.3.1-3.3.3, 3.3.7 Redundant Entry): inline error text tied via aria-describedby and aria-invalid; an error summary with links on submit that moves focus; the technical form is pre-filled from the incident (D/C/R/PM, coordinates, dates) so nothing already entered is re-typed; tri-state Yes/No/Unknown radios start unselected and stack on narrow screens.

Session and timeouts (SC 2.2.1, 2.2.5): warn before expiry, preserve the current URL and unsaved draft across re-authentication, and never discard a form on a network error - keep the token on 5xx and show a retry.

No hover-only affordances; links underlined; every title= value duplicated visibly or in Technical details. The affordance that matters is hand-written CSS at index.css:132, not a Tailwind hover: utility, and it already handles pure touch at index.css:138-142. The residual case is the hybrid pointer - an iPad with a trackpad reports hover: hover while the user taps - and it is covered by making discoverable controls unconditionally visible, not by a media query.

Media and images: photo thumbnails carry alt text from caption and section ('Photo 3 - slope face, looking north'); video and PDF viewers have a visible 'Open in new tab' fallback on iOS where inline preview fails; map legends are real text, not images.

Testing gate for Caltrans and Section 508 review: an automated axe run (wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag22aa) on every route in all three themes at 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px and at 200% and 400% zoom; a manual keyboard walkthrough of the four core paths (coordinator review, hand-off and assign, Staff send, reviewer decide) on desktop and iPad with VoiceOver; and a manual device pass across iPad portrait, landscape, Split View and Stage Manager plus one iPhone and one Android.

Print (brief-research.md:64 names print/PDF parity for long technical inspection forms): the print stylesheet is part of the accessibility surface, not decoration. Printed tri-state answers are words ('Yes' / 'No' / 'Unknown' / 'Not provided'), printed links carry their label, and the print header repeats the record identity on every page.
Minimum text size applies to NAVIGATION LABELS too, which is why the iPad rail label is 12px and not 10px: a primary navigation label is essential text and 10px would violate the plan's own floor.

openQuestions: Should approval auto-resolve the incident report? The sign-off half of this question is CLOSED by the owner: there is no sign-off. Approval ends the assessment and the incident stays open until someone calls /incidents/{id}/resolve, with the workflow tree showing Resolution as CURRENT owned by the assignee, which the plan surfaces honestly with a 'Ready to close out' group. What remains open is only the narrower question: if the policy should be auto-resolve, that is a one-line backend change and it removes a step from every journey.

Can more than one assessment exist per incident? The case file assumes one. If a re-assessment can be opened for the same incident, the 'Who has it' tab needs a selector and the progress rail needs a branch.

Is the submission attachment endpoint callable from the browser origin today (CORS and presigning), or is that a backend task? Until it is, every form and evidence surface says in writing that photos come from the mobile app, and the Staff first-day journey still ends one step short on an iPad browser.

Event Group versus Project on mobile: the mobile triage prompt and the cross-section save dialog both say 'Project' for what the web calls an Event Group. Do we change the mobile strings in the same release, or ship 'Event Group (formerly Project)' for one release?

A district with no DISTRICT_COORDINATOR routing row leaves new reports UNASSIGNED with no notification. The admin System-health strip surfaces it, but should ERIS also refuse to accept a report into an unrouted district, or notify a fallback?
Theme and density persist per browser rather than per account, so on a shared field iPad the last person's choice wins. Should they move to the user record?
How long should 'Recently done by me' stay visible? The plan uses 7 days; coordinators who review weekly may want 14 or 30.
Do we keep three themes? Caltrans Light, Dark and Coastal each triple the contrast verification surface; dropping Coastal would measurably cut Phase 6.
The 60-day return path needs a last_sign_in_at the client can read. B11 adds it to /auth/me - confirm the field exists on the user record, or it becomes a schema change.

Nothing in the current model marks an incident urgent, so every queue in this plan sorts by age. If Caltrans wants a severity or emergency flag driving order, that is a backend field and a new status chip, and it should be decided before Phase 1 sets the sort.

Should a non-assigned Staff member keep the edit access they have today? canEdit (SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:162) is currently ANY FIELD_WORKER or ADMIN on a DRAFT or REJECTED submission, with no assignment check. The technical-form spec narrows it to the assigned Staff member, which both unblocks canonical GEOTECH_ENGINEER accounts (the widening the plan asserts) and locks out Staff covering for each other in the same branch (the narrowing v1.0 was silent about). It is unverified whether the server rejects the narrowed case. Confirm the intent, and whether the server should enforce it.

How big is the 3D terrain payload? The load prompt should name a real figure. No evidence file measures it, so v1.1 removed the 'about 20 MB' that v1.0 shipped as user-facing copy; Phase 4 measures it on the field iPad and puts the number back.

Is users.email the deliverable address for the approval notice? It is the ERIS login. If coordinators sign in with something other than their mailbox, users needs a work_email column (or an external directory lookup) before SMTP_HOST is set anywhere, and B16 cannot deliver until that is answered.

SMTP relay facts for the Caltrans environment: host, port, whether it authenticates, and which From domain it accepts. B16 is shaped for every common answer, but the values are not in the repository, and with no host configured the approval email queues instead of sending.

Does mobile ship in the same release as routing v2? If yes, the two legacy incident-stage assignment endpoints close with it. If mobile lags, POST /incidents/{id}/office-chief/assign-branch must stay live one more release, and a branch-route assessment can still be routed from the app through a path the new rules do not describe.

On the senior engineer route, 'the office chief reviews' is read as the office FUNCTION - any active office chief whose office_code matches the assessment - rather than the individual who made the assignment, because offices have more than one chief, binding to a person would strand the assessment whenever that person is away, and no column records the assigner. Confirm that reading in one line; the alternative is a different rule and a different column.

evidence.decision: A real Not Found screen, not a redirect
